races.name: Charlie Wilson Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Virtuose d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Will lead but 152 days off and pulled up in both hurdle attempts last season raises stamina doubts
runners_data.comment: Huge odds when pulled up in both runs over hurdles last year
runners_data.spotlight: Had a long absence after finishing third in an Irish point and was pulled up in both runs over hurdles last year.

runners_data.name: Mr Finch
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with decent Newbury form but faces traffic problems with four others wanting same position
runners_data.comment: Ran fairly well last time behind two useful novices; this looks easier
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £70,000 after his second in an Irish point; went from the front at Newbury last time (2m4f, good to soft) and ran fairly well behind two useful novices; this looks easier.

runners_data.name: Testing Patience
runners_data.note: Best recent form (RPR 123) but prominent style puts him in the danger zone when field bunches 2-3 out

runners_data.name: Scottish Anthem
runners_data.note: Hold-up style is major tactical advantage; 228 days off flat but solid hurdle debut at Uttoxeter
runners_data.comment: Useful Flat horse who was runner-up on final run over hurdles last summer
runners_data.spotlight: Had plenty of racing on the Flat and ran to a highly respectable level last year at up to 2m; runner-up in his second run over hurdles at Uttoxeter (good) last summer and could run well if fitness doesn't hold him back after a lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Style De Folie
runners_data.note: Prominent style but form is poor (50-1 shot last time) and cheekpieces suggest trainer concerns
runners_data.comment: 50-1 when he finished a long way behind Testing Patience at Fontwell; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: 50-1 when he finished a long way behind Testing Patience at Fontwell; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Lightfingered Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who hasn't progressed since debut but tactical positioning could prove key
runners_data.comment: Hasn't kicked on from his encouraging debut and probably needs to better that form
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't kicked on from his encouraging debut (2m4f, good to soft) and probably needs to better that form to win this; however, it's still days and this gelding has a very appealing jumps pedigree.

runners_data.name: Vanderflier
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who faded in both hurdle starts; wind operation suggests breathing issues addressed
runners_data.comment: Irish point winner; had a wind operation since finishing weakly in both hurdle runs
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £155,000 after winning an Irish point; has finished weakly in both runs over hurdles (2m3f, heavy; 2m7f soft) but interesting that he's since had a wind operation.

runners_data.name: Hay Max
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but beaten 26+ lengths in recent starts including hurdle debut
runners_data.comment: Third on debut; beaten 26l+ in subsequent races, the latest his hurdle debut at Sedgefield
runners_data.spotlight: Best run was the bumper debut at Bangor; beaten 26l+ in his subsequent races, the latest his hurdle debut at Sedgefield (2m4f, good).

runners_data.name: Jorah d'Alma
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tongue-tie first time and Ben Sutton's 5lb claim; won in France over hurdles

runners_data.name: Fullythermal
runners_data.note: Prominent but well held in bumpers and breeding suggests needs much further trips
runners_data.comment: This brother to a 3m5f chase winner is probably one for further down the line
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in both his bumpers and this brother to a 3m5f chase winner is probably one for further down the line.

races.paceDynamic: Virtuose d'Ainay is the sole confirmed front-runner but faces immediate pressure from four prominent runners (Mr Finch, Testing Patience, Style De Folie, Vanderflier, Jorah d'Alma) who will create early congestion behind the leader. This traffic jam will intensify around 2-3 out when the prominent brigade tries to challenge, potentially hampering each other's progress. The hold-up horses (Scottish Anthem, Lightfingered Jack, Hay Max) get a significant tactical advantage as they can avoid the carnage and pick up the pieces in the straight when others have compromised each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses exploit chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners interfere with each other when making their moves 2-3 out
scenarios.body: The traffic problems allow Scottish Anthem and Lightfingered Jack to sweep past tired leaders who've been in a battle. Clean runs from the back prove decisive when the front-runners have been softened up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Testing Patience survives scrum
scenarios.trigger: If Testing Patience can get first run on the prominent pack and avoid trouble
scenarios.body: His superior form figures (RPR 123) tell when he gets a clear passage, overcoming the tactical disadvantage of his prominent style. The hold-up horses don't quite get there in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Virtuose d'Ainay wire-to-wire
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners neutralize each other early and fail to pressure the leader
scenarios.body: The front-runner gets an easy lead and kicks clear before the hold-up horses can organize their challenge. His 152-day break becomes irrelevant with such tactical dominance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jorah d'Alma late surge
scenarios.trigger: If Jorah d'Alma's tongue-tie helps him find extra and he gets the right gaps late
scenarios.body: The French import's best form (won over hurdles in France) emerges with the headgear assistance, timing his run to perfection. Ben Sutton's 5lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch for carnage 2-3 out when Mr Finch, Testing Patience, Vanderflier and Jorah d'Alma all try to challenge simultaneously
Monitor if Virtuose d'Ainay shows any signs of his previous stamina failures that led to pull-ups
Check if Scottish Anthem travels smoothly despite 228-day absence as his hold-up style could be crucial
Observe whether Testing Patience can use his superior form to overcome the tactical disadvantage of prominent positioning
Watch for improvement from Jorah d'Alma with tongue-tie fitted for first time in Britain

races.name: John Sillett Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thank You Ma'am
runners_data.note: Front-running style with uncontested lead ideal for course-and-distance specialist returning to hurdles
runners_data.comment: Exposed but firmly in the mix after his return to form at Wetherby (3m)
runners_data.spotlight: Back hurdling the last twice after a brief stint over fences; the first time he'd worn these aids combined when a front-running third at Wetherby (3m, good; beaten 4.25l); exposed but firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Everyonesgame
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, below-par Ascot run remains a concern
runners_data.comment: Below par last time but repeat of his early-season form wouldn't see him far away
runners_data.spotlight: Below par last time at Ascot but Kempton win in November was off only 4lb lower and then ran fairly well at Cheltenham; if back to that level of form then he wouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: Benign Dictator
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing new blinkers, 33-day break reasonable but hasn't reproduced December course win
runners_data.comment: Course winner in December but hasn't really approached that level since
runners_data.spotlight: Career-best form came here in December when scoring over 3m2f (good to soft); hasn't really approached that level since, in cheekpieces and blinkers (new) the last twice.

runners_data.name: Lipa K
runners_data.note: Hold-up style handicapper facing 179-day absence, career-high mark makes task tougher despite Aintree form
runners_data.comment: A 3lb rise for last time sees him on a career-high mark and he's been off a good while
runners_data.spotlight: Goes particularly well at Bangor but was runner-up at Aintree on final run in October (3m, good); however, a 3lb rise sees him on a career-high mark and he's been off a good while.

runners_data.name: Step Ahead
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose 2m4f Cheltenham win suggests step up in trip will suit perfectly
runners_data.comment: Cheltenham winner who is now raised in trip for his handicap debut; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Second to the smart Moneygarrow here before winning a maiden at Cheltenham (2m4f, good); back on track with a 4l third over 2m5f at Kempton and going further this afternoon could help him on handicap debut; respected.

runners_data.name: J J Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent style, only three runs at 3m but showed he stays when second at Newbury last time
runners_data.comment: Perhaps outbattled at Newbury last time and the cheekpieces could be significant
runners_data.spotlight: Only stepped up to 3m in his last three races and went close in two of those; looked as though he'd win at Newbury last time (good to soft) only to get outbattled; the cheekpieces could be significant.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Ma'am will have an uncontested lead from the start, with Step Ahead and J J Moon settling in behind but neither pressuring the pace early. The front runner can dictate a comfortable gallop over this 3m1f trip, controlling fractions without pressure through the early stages. With four hold-up horses (Everyonesgame, Benign Dictator, Lipa K) sitting well back, the race sets up as a classic front-runner's paradise where Thank You Ma'am can establish position cheaply then kick when ready. This race shape strongly favours the leader and prominent runners who can track the pace without exertion.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Ma'am gets an easy lead and kicks turning for home
scenarios.body: The mare can control every fraction without pressure then use her tactical advantage to repel late challengers. Step Ahead and J J Moon benefit from tracking the winner but can't quite reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Step Ahead or J J Moon apply pressure from 3f out
scenarios.body: The pace quickens significantly in the straight, exposing Thank You Ma'am's stamina while suiting horses with tactical speed. This creates the perfect scenario for a well-positioned tracker to strike late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays very slow and becomes a sprint home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the back markers to close dramatically in the final furlong. Everyonesgame and Benign Dictator benefit most from a truly-run finish where class tells.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lipa K Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the long absence doesn't matter and class surfaces
scenarios.body: The 179-day break proves irrelevant as superior ability shines through in a tactical finish. Lipa K's Aintree second form is the best in the field if reproducible off this layoff.

watchPoints.text: Thank You Ma'am may get too easy a lead early and have enough left to repel all challengers in straight
Lipa K's 179-day absence could prove too much to overcome despite possessing highest-rated recent form
Step Ahead's prominent style perfectly suits this pace setup if he can quicken off steady gallop
Benign Dictator wearing new blinkers suggests connections are concerned about recent below-par efforts
J J Moon's stamina at 3m+ remains question mark with only limited evidence at this extended trip

races.name: Sporting Agenda Challenger Series Mares' Chase Final Handicap Chase (Series Final) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Theonewedreamof
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent Leicester form, 48 days off but Harry Skelton's 20% strike rate suggests readiness
runners_data.comment: Won't mind returning to further and off this mark she's entitled to have a major say
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish mare who has been a bit up and down for Dan Skelton but did run well at Leicecster last time (2m4f, good to soft) given one notable mistake that she made; won't mind returning to further and off this mark she's entitled to have a major say.

runners_data.name: Party Vibes
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won two qualifiers, Henry Daly yard in poor form but this mare shows consistent ability to lead and win
runners_data.comment: Has won two qualifiers for this final this season and yet remains on a competitive mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has won two qualifiers en route to this final, beating a few of these at Cheltenham in December (2m4f, good to soft) and leading late on at Hereford 17 days ago (2m5f, good); remains on a competitive mark despite all that; respected.

runners_data.name: Minniemum
runners_data.note: Last year's winner now 8lb higher, prominent style suits but form has been patchy since that Cheltenham success
runners_data.comment: Won this last year but lacklustre in last three races; hard to support with any confidence
runners_data.spotlight: 8lb higher than for last year's convincing win in this race which was staged at Cheltenham; only subsequent win in six races came at the expense of just three rivals at Ludlow in November (3m1f, good); lacklustre in her last three starts and hard to support with any confidence.

runners_data.name: Kalista Love
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with limited chase experience but Tom Symonds having a decent season, headgear applied
runners_data.comment: Probably has to improve for this longer trip or the application of cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: 2-5 over fences, her latest success when seeing off two other finishers at Fakenham (2m5f, soft) in February; finished behind Holetown at Newbury (2m6f) and needs to improve for this longer trip or the application of cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Kosasiempre
runners_data.note: Stay-on type who was third in last year's final, wind surgery appears to have helped recent form revival
runners_data.comment: Third in last year's final of this series; won over fences and hurdles this campaign
runners_data.spotlight: Third to Minniemum in last year's final of this series; second run after wind surgery when winning over fences at Hereford in November and she added a 3m handicap hurdle last month at Newbury in first-time cheekpieces; solid chance off this mark.

runners_data.name: Realta Liath
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse returning from wind surgery, Warren Greatrex yard struggling but she has the class on her day
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Party Vibes and Theonewedreamof on their Cheltenham clash in December
runners_data.spotlight: Has to bounce back from a couple of modest runs (latest second was a remote one) but she has since undergone a wind operation; closely matched with Party Vibes and Theonewedreamof on their Cheltenham clash in December; possible.

runners_data.name: Ede'iffs Rock
runners_data.note: Front-running mare in career-best form, amateur jockey Darren Andrews takes 7lb off but adds steering concerns
runners_data.comment: In form but a collective 17lb rise for recent Taunton wins could see her vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: 4-10 over fences and better than ever this season with front-running wins at Taunton (2m7f; good to soft/good); this track will suit her style but a collective 17lb rise for those wins could see her vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Lagonda
runners_data.note: Prominent runner now fitted with first-time blinkers after disappointing tailed-off run, probably wants softer conditions
runners_data.comment: Others arrive here in sharper form and this mare probably wants softer ground as well
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkers are turned to after finishing tailed off a month ago and her previous thirds were no great advertisement for her prospects here; probably wants softer ground as well.

runners_data.name: Sunday Soldier
runners_data.note: Hurdle winner struggling over fences, stamina questions over this extended trip despite prominent racing style
runners_data.comment: Multiple hurdle winner who is 0-5 over fences and has a bit to find with some of these
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple hurdle winner who is 0-5 over fences and has a bit to find with some of these; she also has to rebound from a modest effort at Chepstow and her stamina isn't guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Queens Wish
runners_data.note: Bottom weight but has been competing at much lower level, 2lb out of handicap proper makes task even harder
runners_data.comment: 1-8 for current yard and she's been plying her trade at a lower level; 2lb wrong
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Skelton mare who is 1-8 for current yard and she's been plying her trade at a lower level; 2lb out of the weights; others much preferred.

runners_data.name: Holetown
runners_data.note: French import with hold-up style, showed promise when leading late at Ludlow on chase debut over shorter
runners_data.comment: Unraced over this far but wasn't stopping when a 3l third at Newbury
runners_data.spotlight: Dual chase winner in France and was seeing British fences for the first time when leading late on at Ludlow (2m4f, soft); unraced over this far but she wasn't stopping when a 3l third at Newbury (2m6f, good to soft) and she's back against her own sex now; good ground would be a first but provided that's suitable then should make presence felt.

races.paceDynamic: Party Vibes will lead from the start with Ede'iffs Rock, Minniemum, and Lagonda tracking close behind in the early stages. The pace should be genuine but not excessive over this stamina test, with Party Vibes allowed to dictate without serious pressure until the business end. From three out, the prominently-raced horses will come under pressure first, allowing the hold-up performers like Theonewedreamof, Kalista Love, and Holetown to unleash their finishing kicks. This pace dynamic strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the extended trip and benefit from a solid gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays honest but not excessive, allowing strong finishers to close
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will set up perfectly for horses coming from behind, with stamina reserves proving crucial in the final furlong. Theonewedreamof and Holetown have the class and tactical profile to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Rank Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Party Vibes or Ede'iffs Rock get away with a controlled pace up front
scenarios.body: The leaders will have enough left in reserve to resist late challenges, particularly if the ground doesn't deteriorate. Party Vibes' recent course form and Ede'iffs Rock's front-running prowess make them dangerous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Proves Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or becomes stop-start, neutralising finishing kicks
scenarios.body: Horses positioned in fourth to sixth will find themselves ideally placed when the race develops, avoiding pace problems. Minniemum's class and Kosasiempre's stamina could prove decisive from these positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Party Vibes goes too slow early and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace will turn this into a tactical affair where any horse with a turn of foot can win. Queens Wish at the bottom of the weights or an improving type like Sunday Soldier could steal it.

watchPoints.text: Party Vibes sets fractions that are too strong early and compounds into the straight, destroying her finishing kick
Ede'iffs Rock's amateur rider Darren Andrews makes tactical errors at crucial jumping obstacles in the home straight
Theonewedreamof and Holetown get too far back in the early stages and leave themselves impossible tasks from the rear
Minniemum travels strongly into contention but fails to quicken under pressure like she did when winning this last year
The pace becomes tactical early with Party Vibes going too slow, turning this into a sprint finish that favours different profiles

races.name: KTDA Mares' Challenger Series Final Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Siog Geal
runners_data.note: Proven at this level with strong recent form, prominent style suits the predicted pace shape perfectly
runners_data.comment: Has had another good campaign off her tough mark and went down narrowly last time
runners_data.spotlight: Had Pismo Beach in third when winning last season's mares' final at Newbury (2m4f, good); has had another good campaign off her tough mark and went down narrowly last time at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) with Fern O'Brien claiming her 5lb; back up 1lb; each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Pretending
runners_data.note: Back to form last time after disappointing runs, forward position crucial given expected traffic problems
runners_data.comment: Third last year; made a handy return to form when winning at Market Rasen
runners_data.spotlight: Third to Greyval 12 months ago off the same mark; hadn't been at her best this season but came good at Market Rasen (2m4f, soft) and clearly capable of having some say in the outcome.

runners_data.name: Rula Bula
runners_data.note: Form tailing off this season, needs to bounce back from recent Cheltenham disappointment
runners_data.comment: Last season started well but petered out and it might be happening again
runners_data.spotlight: Last season started well but petered out and it might be happening again, as although it wasn't a bad run behind Cheltenham Festival heroine White Noise two starts back, Chepstow last time was underwhelming (well behind Siog Geal; soft ground no excuse).

runners_data.name: Rockola Vogue
runners_data.note: Hold-up style problematic given expected pace scenario, recent form plateau concerning
runners_data.comment: Progress has stalled since early-season wins and looks on a hard mark
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up two handicaps in the autumn (2m3f/2m7f, good) but her progress has rather stalled since then and looks on a hard mark.

runners_data.name: Hard Dealt
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter but limited winning ability, prominent position offers tactical hope
runners_data.comment: Has only won a Worcester novice and failed in six handicaps off lower marks
runners_data.spotlight: Has only won a Worcester novice and failed in six handicaps off lower marks, though was runner-up in four of those; clearly has nothing up her sleeve mark-wise but should still run well.

runners_data.name: Greyval
runners_data.note: Defending champion returning from 78-day break, hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner; plenty in her favour for a bold defence with cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race last year (at Cheltenham) off today's mark; turned her back on chasing this winter and ran quite well over 3m at Kempton before finding soft ground too testing at Ludlow; plenty looks in her favour this time with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Audacious Annie
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner facing no pace pressure, 95-day absence and cheekpieces first-time previously
runners_data.comment: Good record here but appears to have little margin for error off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: First and second in her two previous visits here, latterly over this far in first-time cheekpieces in November; below best in her last two races (3m/2m4f) and appears to have little margin for error off this mark; absent since January.

runners_data.name: Pismo Beach
runners_data.note: Classy Grade 2 performer but hold-up style poorly suited to expected pace dynamics
runners_data.comment: Possibly a career best when second to a talented mare at Newbury last time
runners_data.spotlight: Placed for a second time in last month's Grade 2 mares' novices handicap at Newbury (good to soft), this season beating all bar the talented Charisma Cat who went on to run well in a Grade 1 at Aintree; bumped up 4lb for that but this mare will enjoy the good ground; chance.

runners_data.name: Crazierthandaisy
runners_data.note: Inconsistent performer despite quality connections, hold-up tactics create uphill task
runners_data.comment: 5lb above only mark she's defied in a handicap and a 7lb claimer was employed last time
runners_data.spotlight: Looked a bit unlucky not to win at Uttoxeter last time (2m4f, good to soft) but wouldn't be certain to run as well again given her inconsistency; 5lb above the only mark she's defied in a handicap and a 7lb claimer was employed last time.

runners_data.name: Keep On Cobbling
runners_data.note: Limited handicapper whose hold-up style faces significant tactical obstacles
runners_data.comment: Soft going perhaps not ideal the last time and this 6yo is bred to improve with her racing
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner who made a successful handicap debut at Sedgefield (2m5f, good) but hasn't advanced her form from there; however, soft ground perhaps not ideal the last time and this 6yo is bred to improve with her racing.

runners_data.name: Service Minimum
runners_data.note: Fresh from recent win but hold-up approach disadvantageous given pace setup
runners_data.comment: An 11lb rise for her Bangor win asks major questions in this loftier grade
runners_data.spotlight: Would have found conditions too soft when seventh behind Pretending at Market Rasen and she then justified market confidence with a narrow win at Bangor (2m3f, good); she travelled much the best in that race but the handicapper went with an 11lb rise and that asks major questions in this loftier grade.

runners_data.name: Country Mouse
runners_data.note: Prominent style helps tactically but limited ability at this level of competition
runners_data.comment: 3rd in a novice in December; lesser runs have followed, including handicap debut when 25-1
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner; the Ludlow third in December (2m5f novice; good to soft) offers some hope off this mark but lesser runs have followed, including her handicap debut when a 25-1 chance; cheekpieces added.

races.paceDynamic: Audacious Annie will lead from the start with no genuine pace rival, creating a controlled tempo over the first circuit. Five horses (Siog Geal, Pretending, Rula Bula, Hard Dealt, Country Mouse) will bunch up prominently behind the leader, creating traffic congestion approaching the final three hurdles. The hold-up brigade (Rockola Vogue, Greyval, Pismo Beach, Crazierthandaisy, Keep On Cobbling, Service Minimum) will have ground to make up in the straight. This moderate early pace followed by prominent crowding strongly favours front-running tactics and horses positioned closest to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Audacious Annie Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If the leader maintains her advantage through the congestion and isn't headed approaching the last
scenarios.body: Audacious Annie gets first run on the field while the prominent pack interfere with each other, allowing her to build an unassailable lead despite her long absence. Her two previous course wins prove she handles Warwick's demands when dictating terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If the bunch behind Audacious Annie produces the winner from their traffic battle
scenarios.body: The five prominent runners create their own mini-race within a race, with the classiest among them (Siog Geal or Pretending) fighting clear of the scrimmaging. Their forward positions give them crucial tactical advantage over the hold-up horses who face an impossible task.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and allows a closer to sweep past the tiring leaders
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop plays into the hands of a classy hold-up performer who can quicken late despite giving ground away early. Pismo Beach or Crazierthandaisy could benefit if their jockeys time their run perfectly through gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Audacious Annie sets crawling fractions and gets headed by multiple challengers in the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure creates a bunched field turning for home, leading to a cavalry charge finish. This scenario requires perfect jumping and positioning from the eventual winner as gaps become scarce.

watchPoints.text: Audacious Annie could steal this if she gets soft fractions early and the field allows her to dictate completely unchallenged
Traffic chaos developing 2-3 hurdles from home as five prominent runners (Siog Geal, Pretending, Rula Bula, Hard Dealt, Country Mouse) converge simultaneously
Greyval returning from 78-day layoff as defending champion, any market confidence suggests hidden fitness work
Pismo Beach and Crazierthandaisy need significant pace collapse to overcome their hold-up disadvantage
Service Minimum's recent Bangor win came on good ground, suggesting she handles today's conditions better than her Market Rasen flop

races.name: Vanessa Littler's 60th Birthday Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Blackijo Dagrostis
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 29 days off who made a late mistake at Taunton but disappointed behind Ballywood last time, making him hard to recommend here.
runners_data.comment: Good penultimate effort but Hereford was disappointing when behind Ballywood
runners_data.spotlight: 13-race maiden; late mistake cost him dear at Taunton two runs back (2m, good) but Hereford was disappointing when behind Ballywood; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Zoeman
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer switching to fences this season with three good runs before flopping in cheekpieces, now back without them after 77 days.
runners_data.comment: Three good runs over fences before flopping in first-time cheekpieces that are now removed
runners_data.spotlight: Switched to fences this season and produced three good runs in defeat (2m-2m4f) before flopping in first-time cheekpieces when made favourite at Huntingdon in early February; could be given another chance with that headgear swiftly removed.

runners_data.name: Ballywood
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who gets easy leads and nearly won at Huntingdon but was spent early at Hereford, benefits from Worsley's 5lb claim.
runners_data.comment: Hasn't won a race for years and may need an easy lead for him to put that right
runners_data.spotlight: Nearly won for the first time in seven years at Huntingdon (2m, good) but he got an easy lead then and he was a spent force some way out at Hereford; wouldn't be the percentage call.

runners_data.name: Kally Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse moving up in grade after narrow chase win at Market Rasen, dual hurdle winner who may still be improving over fences.
runners_data.comment: Made all last time; up in grade off 5lb higher and there could be competition for the lead

races.paceDynamic: Ballywood is the only confirmed front-runner and will get an uncontested lead from flag to finish, setting a moderate gallop that won't stretch the field early. With eight hold-up horses tracking behind including Zoeman, Forcetoreckonwith and Kally Des Bruyeres, this becomes a tactical affair where positioning and timing matter more than raw pace. The lack of early pressure allows patient riders to deliver late challenges, but Ballywood's soft lead gives him every chance to resist. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can quicken late, as they'll face minimal early pace and can time their runs to perfection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Ballywood gets his preferred soft lead and jumps cleanly throughout.
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old controls the tempo completely and has enough left to resist late challenges, particularly with his recent Huntingdon near-miss showing retained ability. His 149lbs burden and Tabitha Worsley's 5lb claim make him hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of early pace allows multiple hold-up horses to arrive with winning chances.
scenarios.body: Forcetoreckonwith and Zoeman benefit most from the tactical setup, with their proven chase form and patient riding styles perfectly suited to a finish where several can win. The stronger finishers overcome Ballywood's early advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving Chaser Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Kally Des Bruyeres' recent Market Rasen win signals genuine progress over fences.
scenarios.body: The six-year-old's dual hurdle wins and narrow chase success show he's still improving, and Tom Bellamy can position him perfectly behind the slow pace. His grade rise looks manageable given his upward trajectory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the tactical nature and good ground allows a longer-priced runner to outfinish the favourites.
scenarios.body: Lunar Ocean or Blackijo Dagrostis profit from being overlooked while getting ideal race conditions, with their patient styles suiting the setup perfectly. The even pace exposes class differences less than usual.

watchPoints.text: Ballywood must be monitored for early jumping errors as any mistake will compromise his front-running tactics and hand the initiative to patient followers.
Zoeman's first run without cheekpieces after 77 days off needs close attention, as his Huntingdon flop suggests the headgear change affected him negatively.
Ironica De Thaix has shown fading tendencies and pulled up last time, making her a potential non-completion risk in this longer chase.
The pace will be crucial to monitor early as Ballywood's uncontested lead could become either a winning advantage or energy-sapping liability.
Several hold-up horses including Forcetoreckonwith and Kally Des Bruyeres will need clear runs in the straight to deliver their best finishing kicks.

races.paceDynamic: Inion Tiogair, Midnight View, and Pottersjetamay will ensure a strong early gallop over this stamina-testing 2m3f trip at Warwick. Inion Tiogair has been making all recently at Chepstow, while Midnight View showed early speed in his placed efforts, and Pottersjetamay consistently forces the pace. This sustained gallop will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the final half-mile. The strong pace heavily favours hold-up horses and prominent runners with proven stamina, as early leaders will struggle to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and weaken markedly
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses to pick off the pace-setters in the final furlong. Bannister, Snapius, and Killycarn all have the tactical speed to capitalize when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Inion Tiogair can control the tempo and kick clear
scenarios.body: Her recent Chepstow wins show she can dictate and maintain, especially with the step up to this stamina-testing trip suiting. Orange Diamond could track and challenge late having won over similar distances.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Son Of Hypnos or Can't Resist It can sit close and pounce
scenarios.body: The strong pace will soften up the leaders perfectly for horses that can race prominently without leading. Both have shown they can finish strongly when positioned just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start with leaders going too slow
scenarios.body: Without the expected strong gallop, horses with natural speed like Pottersjetamay could dominate from the front. This would compromise the hold-up horses who need a true test of stamina.

watchPoints.text: Inion Tiogair could set too strong a pace early and compromise her own finishing effort despite recent wins
Pottersjetamay's 17lb weight allowance makes him dangerous if he can control the tempo from the front
Snapius returning quickly from his Huntingdon win could be primed for another bold showing
Several horses returning from lengthy breaks including Bannister (161 days) and Orange Diamond (91 days)
Multiple first-time headgear changes including Ballynorth's hood and Major Major's blinkers switch

races.paceDynamic: Roger Rarebit and Caterpillar Girl will contest the early lead, with Sleeping Satellite likely to track close behind given his prominent style. The pace should be honest but not overly demanding over 2m4f with three natural front-runners in the field. Moonshine Man will also be handy early, creating a solid gallop that should set up the race nicely. This tactical setup clearly favours the hold-up horses who can sit off the pace and deliver late kicks, as the leaders will have done plenty of work by the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners Roger Rarebit and Caterpillar Girl go too hard early and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The honest pace will weaken the leaders approaching the final fence, allowing the patient hold-up horses to sweep past with fresher finishing kicks. Two To Tango and Move With The Beat are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario with their proven late-running styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Rarebit can establish a clear lead and dictate fractions without serious pressure from Caterpillar Girl
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old's class and course form will tell as he strings out the field with controlled front-running. His recent consistency and proven ability at the trip makes him dangerous if allowed his own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Sleeping Satellite can sit just behind the leaders and time his challenge perfectly approaching the last
scenarios.body: His dual make-all wins in autumn show he has the tactical speed to quicken, and tracking the pace allows him to avoid the early battle while staying close enough to pounce. Moonshine Man's similar prominent style could also profit from this patient approach.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a messy scramble with multiple fallers or a crawling pace that negates class
scenarios.body: The handicapper's dream scenario where form gets turned upside down and an improving type can spring a surprise. Claim Du Brizais showed his best chase form here last time and could capitalize on any confusion.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Roger Rarebit and Caterpillar Girl going too fast early and compromising each other's chances
Monitor how quickly Two To Tango and Move With The Beat can get into contention from their hold-up positions
Observe whether Sleeping Satellite chooses to lead or track the pace given his tactical flexibility
Check if Moonshine Man shows any ring-rustiness after his 80-day layoff when the pace quickens
Note how Claim Du Brizais handles the likely strong gallop given his progressive chase form here last time
